title: Filter a query-only list
summary: WHERE chooses rows that pass a rule. A WITH list gives this practice query its own small dataset.
introduction: WHERE chooses rows that pass a rule. A WITH list gives this practice query its own small dataset. Your task: Change the minimum to 10.
learningObjectives: Explain the example for filter a query-only list

blocks.text: WHERE chooses rows that pass a rule. A WITH list gives this practice query its own small dataset.
Use the SQL Run button for examples marked runnable. They use this site's in-browser SQLite database and sample-only table names. A Python example needs Python on your own computer instead.

blocks.code:
WITH books(title,pages) AS (VALUES('Moon Trip',60),('Tiny Seed',20))
SELECT title FROM books WHERE pages>=50;
blocks.title: Filter a query-only list

blocks.text: Read the code step by step

items: `SELECT` names the output values. `AS` can give a calculated result a readable column name.
`WHERE` keeps only rows that pass its condition. Check the condition with sample data before using it for a change.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: Use single quotes around SQL text. A number such as 50 does not need quotes.
